toegepas.rede_vinder: Fronting 'Ook' is stiff; 'Dit is ook vals' is the natural order at this grade.
toegepas.fout: Fronted 'Ook dit' is stiff and bookish for a Grade 6 reader.
toegepas.rede_keurder: 'Dit is ook vals' is the natural spoken order and says exactly the same thing.

toegepas.rede_vinder: 'Uitsorteer' calques English 'sort out'; the meaning here is to recognise the myths, which is 'uitken'.
toegepas.fout: 'uitsorteer' in the sense of 'figure out' copies English 'sort out'.
toegepas.rede_keurder: 'uitken' is the natural Afrikaans verb for recognising the myths as myths, and the meaning stays the same.

toegepas.voor: van 'n ma na haar baba, en deur seks
toegepas.na: van 'n ma na haar baba en deur seks
toegepas.rede_vinder: AWS 2017: no comma before 'en' in a list.
toegepas.fout: Comma before 'en' in a three-item list of routes.
toegepas.rede_keurder: AWS 2017 and the house rule: no comma before 'en' in a list; the three routes still read clearly.

laat_vaar.voor: glo MIV gaan oor deur 'n drukkie, 'n beker of 'n muskietbyt
laat_vaar.na: glo MIV gaan deur 'n drukkie, 'n beker of 'n muskietbyt oor
laat_vaar.rede_vinder: The separable verb 'oorgaan' puts 'oor' at the end of the clause, as the lesson itself does in 'MIV gaan nie deur 'n drukkie of 'n beker oor nie'.
laat_vaar.rede_keurder: Placing 'oor' before a long prepositional list is normal Afrikaans, and the next block uses the same order ('MIV gaan oor deur bloed, ...'), so the change is lateral and would make the two blocks differ.

laat_vaar.voor: help wel mense om gesond te bly
laat_vaar.na: help mense wel om gesond te bly
laat_vaar.rede_vinder: The modal particle 'wel' sits more naturally after the object 'mense'.
laat_vaar.rede_keurder: 'wel' before an indefinite object reads naturally already; moving it is a lateral move.

laat_vaar.voor: as hulle beddegoed of klere vat
laat_vaar.na: as hulle beddegoed of klere hanteer
laat_vaar.rede_vinder: 'Vat' is colloquial for handling soiled items; 'hanteer' is clearer and still grade-appropriate.
laat_vaar.rede_keurder: 'vat' is plain, clear Afrikaans for a Grade 6 reader in the glove-use wording, which was checked as content; 'hanteer' only reads more formal.

laat_vaar.voor: 'n Kind help op gewone maniere by die huis
laat_vaar.na: 'n Kind kan op gewone maniere by die huis help
laat_vaar.rede_vinder: The bare present reads as a statement of fact about every child; 'kan ... help' matches the following 'Jy kan' sentences and reads naturally.
laat_vaar.rede_keurder: Adding 'kan' changes a statement about the child's role (beside the adults' care) into a possibility; the generic present is natural and the meaning would move.

laat_vaar.blok: Wie sorg, het ook hulp nodig
laat_vaar.voor: Dalk moet jy self te veel van die sorg dra
laat_vaar.na: Dalk dra jy self te veel van die sorg
laat_vaar.rede_vinder: 'Dalk moet jy ... dra' can be misread as advice that the child should carry too much; 'Dalk dra jy' states the situation without that ambiguity.
laat_vaar.rede_keurder: 'moet' says the child is made to carry too much of the care, and 'te veel' rules out reading it as advice; dropping 'moet' loses that sense.

vlae.blok: MIV en VIGS is nie dieselfde nie
vlae.teks: Die medisyne keer dit by die meeste mense wat dit elke dag drink.
vlae.rede: 'Die medisyne' has no earlier antecedent in the lesson, and the two 'dit's refer to different things (VIGS, then the medicine); the protected phrase blocks a rewrite of the second half, so a writer should decide whether the opening needs a clearer reference.
